research_rationale:
Executive Order 13599 of 2012-02-05 (77 FR 6659, PDF pages 1-4) is held as the Federal Register original (govinfo PDF text layer, grade official original). I read it in full and confirm its identity and its clause inventory of 24 scopes as prepared (a dup2 suffix distinguishes repeated item labels in different subsections). Its authority is IEEPA, the NEA and the other statutes it names, and it rests on the national emergency declared on March 15, 1995 in Executive Order 12957, on which Executive Order 13599 states it relies. Notice of March 2, 2026 (91 FR 10937; FR Doc. 2026-04450) states that the emergency must continue in effect beyond March 15, 2026, so the emergency, and the order that depends on it, were in effect on the cutoff of 2026-10-14 (NEA section 202(d)). Earlier annual continuation notices for the same emergency are also held; the latest one is relied on because it speaks as of its date. The held original has no own-terms end, expiry or sunset. I read the coverage notes of current-law:usc (U.S. Code release point through 2026-10-09), current-law:ecfr (as of 2026-10-14) and later-events:ofr_catalog (checked 2026-11-25); they show no revocation, supersession or partial revocation of this order. The Federal Register disposition notes for this order contain cross-reference entries only, naming EO 12170, EO 12281, EO 12957, EO 13628 and the Notice of March 2, 2026, none of which is stated to revoke or supersede this order. No later instrument amends or revokes any clause. The dossier gaps listed as NOTICE identities absent from the census are annual continuation notices and cross-references, not events that change this order; the current-law pointer gaps concern CFR and Code pointers that this claim does not rely on, because the conclusion rests on the order's own text and the continuation notice. The acting-text lead for Executive Order 14294 (Fighting Overcriminalization in Federal Regulations, May 9, 2025) was checked: a scan of the held corpus found no mention of this order in its text, so no provision targeting this order was located. EO 13645 of June 3, 2013 and EO 13846 of August 6, 2018 refer to property blocked solely pursuant to this order; they presuppose it and neither amends nor revokes it. Sections 10 and 11 delegate functions under section 1245(d) of the NDAA; the current text of that statutory section is not separately held, no held source repeals or limits it, and the claim treats the delegations as continuing because no held source ends them. Savings: none arises because the order remained in force at the cutoff.
